query: Given a sorted list of integers, find two numbers that add up to a target without using extra memory beyond constant space.
Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place and return the new length, overwriting elements as we scan from both indices.
Check whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards by comparing characters moving inward from the two ends using two pointers.
Find the longest contiguous substring that contains no repeated characters, while scanning the input once from left to right.
Compute the maximum sum of any k consecutive elements in an array of numbers, updating the running total as the range moves.
Return the smallest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least a given positive threshold, expanding and shrinking the window as needed.
We receive thousands of queries asking for the sum of elements between index l and r on a static array; each must answer fast.
Count the number of contiguous subarrays whose elements sum exactly to k, where values may be negative, using cumulative totals and a lookup.
Precompute cumulative sums so that range sum queries on an immutable array run in constant time after linear preprocessing, a prefix sum approach.
Locate a value in a sorted array in logarithmic time and return its index, or minus one when it is absent.
Find the minimum capacity of a conveyor that ships all packages within D days, where feasibility is monotonic in the capacity.
A sorted array was rotated at an unknown pivot; find a target value in it in O(log n) by halving the search range.
Given an unsorted array and a target, return the indices of two numbers adding up to it in a single pass.
Group words that are anagrams of each other by building a canonical key per word and collecting words under the same key.
Count how often each element occurs in a large list and report the first value seen twice, using a dictionary for constant lookups.
Detect whether a singly linked list contains a cycle without using extra memory or marking visited nodes.
Find the middle node of a singly linked list in one traversal, without first computing its length.
Given a linked list with a loop, return the node where the cycle begins using the tortoise and hare technique.
Validate that a string of brackets such as parentheses, square and curly braces is properly nested and every opener is closed in order.
Evaluate a postfix arithmetic expression given as tokens, pushing operands and applying each operator to the most recent two values.
Implement an undo feature for an editor where the most recently performed action is always the first one reverted, last in first out.
For each day in a temperature series, compute how many days you must wait until a warmer day, in linear time.
For every element in an array find the next greater element to its right, scanning once and keeping candidates in decreasing order.
Find the area of the largest rectangle in a histogram of bar heights by tracking bars with increasing heights on a monotonic stack.
Return the k largest elements from a stream of numbers while keeping only k items in memory at any time.
Merge k already sorted lists into a single sorted list by repeatedly extracting the smallest head element among all lists.
Maintain a running median of a data stream where numbers arrive one at a time, using two heaps balanced against each other.
Find the minimum number of moves to get from the start cell to the exit in an unweighted grid maze with walls.
Given an unweighted graph, compute the fewest edges between a source node and every other node, exploring level by level with a queue.
Transform one word into another by changing a single letter at a time through dictionary words, finding the shortest transformation sequence length.
Count the number of separate islands in a grid of land and water cells by exploring each connected region recursively.
Visit every node reachable from a starting vertex by following edges as deep as possible and then backing up, recording visit order.
Detect whether a directed graph has a cycle by tracking which nodes are on the current recursion path during a depth first walk.
Given a stream of friendships between people, determine how many separate friend groups exist after each new connection is added.
Detect the redundant edge in an undirected graph that closes a cycle, by checking whether both endpoints already belong to the same component.
Merge account records that share any email address into groups, using a disjoint set structure with path compression and union by rank.
Given courses with prerequisites, decide whether all courses can be completed and output a valid order to take them.
Order build tasks so every task runs only after the tasks it depends on, and report an error when dependencies form a cycle.
Produce a linear ordering of the vertices of a directed acyclic graph such that every edge goes from earlier to later, via in-degree counting.
Find the cheapest route between two cities on a road network where every road has a non-negative travel time.
Compute the minimum delay for a signal to reach all nodes in a weighted directed graph with positive edge weights from a given source.
Shortest path from one source in a weighted graph with no negative edges, using a priority queue to always expand the closest unsettled node.
Compute cheapest paths from a source in a weighted graph where some edges have negative costs, and flag any negative cycle reachable from it.
Find the cheapest flight from origin to destination using at most k stops, relaxing all edges repeatedly for k plus one rounds.
Detect arbitrage in currency exchange rates by looking for a negative cycle after taking logarithms, relaxing every edge up to V minus one times.
Given a list of meeting start and end times, find the largest number of meetings one room can host without any overlapping.
Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so that the remaining intervals do not overlap, sorting by finishing time first.
Merge all overlapping time ranges in a list into the smallest set of non-overlapping ranges, after sorting them by start.
Generate all subsets of a list of distinct numbers, building each candidate step by step and undoing the last choice after recursion.
Place n queens on a chessboard so that none attack each other, and return every valid arrangement found by exploring and pruning.
Enumerate every permutation of a collection of elements, choosing an unused item at each position and then unchoosing it to try alternatives.
A climber can take one or two steps at a time; count the distinct ways to reach the top of n stairs.
Given house values along a street, maximize the loot without robbing two adjacent houses, using a table indexed by position.
Find the fewest coins needed to make up an amount given unlimited denominations, building answers for smaller amounts first in a single array.
Compute the length of the longest common subsequence between two strings using a table indexed by prefix lengths of each.
Find the minimum number of insert, delete and replace operations to turn one word into another, filling a grid of subproblem results.
Count unique paths from the top left to the bottom right of a grid with obstacles, moving only right or down.
Build an autocomplete feature that returns every stored word starting with the characters a user has typed so far.
Implement a dictionary supporting insert, exact word lookup and checking whether any stored word begins with a given prefix, sharing common leading characters.
Store a large set of words in a prefix tree so we can search for words with a wildcard character quickly.
Find every position where a pattern occurs in a long text in linear time, including overlapping matches, avoiding re-comparing characters after a mismatch.
Precompute the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix for each position of a pattern, then use it to skip ahead on mismatch.
Locate substring occurrences in guaranteed O(n plus m) time without ever backing up in the text, the way KMP does.
